summary: Valeria Gazizova works in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Oslo, completing a master's thesis supervised by Per Kvaerne, and was also taught by Hanna Havnevik.

Van Austin Harvey was a religious studies scholar who studied at Occidental College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Yale University. He taught at Princeton, Southern Methodist University, and the University of Pennsylvania before serving as a professor at Stanford University.
Vans Kennedy was an Indologist and linguist. He served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army (1817–1835) and as president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1846).

Vasant Shivram Shinde is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts as Professor and Professor of South Asian Archaeology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2006 and 2026).

Vasily Mikhaylovich Alekseyev was a sinologist who studied at St. Petersburg University and under Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1910–1951), the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1921–1951), and the National Library of Russia (1924–1926).

Sinologist and Tibetologist Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev studied at Kazan Federal University under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski. He served as professor at Kazan Federal University (1851) and at Saint Petersburg State University (1855, in charge 1878–1893).

Vasily Radlov was a linguist and archaeologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Jena. He directed the Asiatic Museum (1885–1890) and the Peter the Great Museum of Anthropology and Ethnography / Kunstkamera (1894–1918).

Philosopher Vasily Seseman studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1903–1909). He subsequently held academic posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1915–1919), Vytautas Magnus University (~1923–1940), and Vilnius University (~1940–1963).

Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned his PhD from the University of Bonn. He held academic posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi (attested 1966).

Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi was an Indologist and historian who studied at Deccan College and the University of Mumbai. He served as Principal of Morris College and Vidarbha Institute, and later as professor at Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University (1957–1966).

Indologist and historian Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Lucknow. He was curator at the Mathura Museum, director of the State Museum, Lucknow, and head of Indology at Banaras Hindu University (1951).

Indologist Vasudha Dalmia studied at Miranda House, the University of Cologne, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Heidelberg University. She lectured at the University of Tübingen and served as professor at UC Berkeley (2001–2012) and Yale University (2013–2014).

Vasudha Narayanan is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the Universities of Madras and Mumbai, and Harvard University. She founded the University of Florida, where she became Distinguished Professor of Religion (~1982).

Linguist Vatroslav Jagić studied at the University of Vienna (~1856–1860). He held posts at Odesa University (~1871–1873), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1874–1880), Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1880–1886), and the University of Vienna (~1886–1908).

Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi works in Indology and philosophy. After studying at Central and National Sanskrit Universities, he held posts at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha, the French Institute of Pondicherry, Rajasthan Sanskrit University, and Karnataka Samskrit University.

Velcheru Narayana Rao is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Sir C. R. Reddy College, Andhra University, and Osmania University. He served as a lecturer and associate professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (from 1971).

Vempati Kutumba Sastry is an Indologist. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the Central Sanskrit University (2003–2008) and as president of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (~2006–2018).

Verity Harte is a philosopher who studied at the University of Cambridge. She held research posts at St Edmund's College and St Hilda's College, taught at King's College London, and was named professor at Yale University in 2006.
Verrier Elwin was an Indologist and historian who studied at Dean Close School and Merton College. He served as the first deputy director of the Anthropological Survey of India (~1946–1949).

Vesna A. Wallace is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed her doctorate at UC Berkeley. She held the Numata Chair at the University of Oxford and served as professor and department chair at UC Santa Barbara.
